facts.fact: 插页遗书：最苦的不是孤独也不是黑暗，是「有人会转角来救我」的希望。
facts.anchor: The loneliness isn’t the worst part of being lost down here. Not the darkness either. It’s the hope. The hope that someeone will round the corner and save me. I want to end it. But I can’t. Because of that damn hope.

facts.fact: 入水瞬间冷透衣物，她强迫自己睁眼确认两人在前方。
facts.anchor: The water hits like ice, the cold immediately penetrating the fabric of my clothing. It stings when I open my eyes, but I have to make sure Jade and Flint are in front of me.

facts.fact: 她靠想「植物学」压 panic：海草靠把 Void Core 能量转成食物的 chemosynthesis 活着。
facts.anchor: Seagrass grows out of the sand beneath me. They live on a form of chemosynthesis in which they convert energy from the Void Core into food, and the thought of these little plants converting nitrogen and CO2 into energy by means of some complicated process I can’t begin to grasp helps quell my panic.

facts.fact: 窄道夹住她的髋部，她自嘲若死于自己的屁股实在太惨。
facts.anchor: I squeeze through the narrow passage, the rocky walls gripping my hips and keeping me from moving forward. Come on. How sad would it be if my thick ass was the cause of my death.

facts.fact: Jade 把头没入水面，与她对上眼时神情松下来。
facts.anchor: Jade dunks her head beneath the surface, her face relaxing when we lock eyes.

facts.fact: Flint 确认这正是他要的那条：有通往第四层的水下通道。
facts.anchor: “This is the tunnel I thought it was,” Flint says proudly. “So, we had nothing to worry about. There’s an underwater passage that leads down to the Fourth Layer.

facts.fact: 被碰一下脚就让她以为 Cadaver Giant 的手链在拖她，直接窜上岩岛。
facts.anchor: Something brushes my foot⁠—just a fish, but the image of the Cadaver Giant’s chain of hands dragging me underwater sends me flying onto the slippery rock with Jade.

facts.fact: 她暗自庆幸走了水下通道——没人会知道她逃跑时尿了裤子。
facts.anchor: now no one will ever know I pissed myself while we were running from the Cadaver Giant.

facts.fact: 她的光照到一只睡袋，拉开时带下一具半融在布里的腐尸，脸皮随之剥落。
facts.anchor: My light shines on something big wrapped in a nylon bundle a few feet from us. I crawl closer to it. It’s a sleeping bag, the same kind of water-resistant one that I bought at Mr. Stone’s. I pull back on the fabric, but it’s stuck to something. I pull harder, revealing a decomposing corpse half fused to the fabric, some of his face peeling away with the sleeping bag.

facts.fact: Flint 判断这具尸体的肌肉消耗方式说明他靠此地之物活了数周，大概吃海草。
facts.anchor: “The way his muscles have wasted,” Flint continues, studying the body, a heaviness in his voice, “I’d say he managed to survive on something around here for weeks. Probably ate the seaweed.

I experienced that for about thirty minutes and was on the brink of total mental collapse. There’s no way I could’ve held on like this guy. I’d probably drown myself, but there would always be that question

facts.fact: 她自陈：同样的黑暗她只撑了约三十分钟就濒临全面崩溃，却断定自己若落此地总会存着「也许有人来救」的疑问。
facts.anchor: I experienced that for about thirty minutes and was on the brink of total mental collapse. There’s no way I could’ve held on like this guy. I’d probably drown myself, but there would always be that question: What if someone’s coming to save me?

facts.fact: 死者包里有一本旅行版《The Unspoken Truth of the Void》——Jade 和 Petra 从不信 surfacewalker 传闻，所以从没翻过这类书。
facts.anchor: One of them is the travel edition of The Unspoken Truth of the Void. I’ve seen the full version before, in one of the shops. It’s a tome that I’ve never bothered reading, since Jade and I don’t believe in any of the surfacewalker rumors.

facts.fact: Jade 朗读迷信条目：surfacewalker 原是 Obscuris 居民，被诅咒变成了 Void 生物。
facts.anchor: Surfacewalkers were once citizens of Obscuris but were cursed and turned into Void creatures.

facts.fact: 续读：只要献上一个活人祭品，女神就会赐 surfacewalker 新皮。
facts.anchor: The Goddess will bless a surfacewalker with a new skin, but only if she is brought a human sacrifice.
Number two, don’t trust anyone you haven’t known since birth. Jeez, Pet, I guess you shouldn’t be here

facts.fact: Flint 抢回书放回死者身边，说「别嘲笑死人，这家伙比你聪明」。
facts.anchor: Flint snatches the book from Jade, putting it back with the dead diver’s other belongings. “You shouldn’t mock the dead. And this guy was smarter than you are.

facts.fact: Flint 表态他不拜「女神」，但认为 Void Truthers 是唯一在问对问题的人；Petra 心里骂他傲慢。
facts.anchor: But Void Truthers are the only ones asking the right questions about this place.”

facts.fact: Petra 提旧事（Jade 募捐时被抢硬币），Flint 直呼她在撒谎。
facts.anchor: “At least Jade never stole from you,” I mumble.

facts.fact: Jade 反驳：那是多年前的白天，他不曾挨饿所以忘了。
facts.anchor: “I’m not lying,” Jade says firmly. “It was years ago, but I remember that day more than you do. You never had to go hungry, so of course you forgot.

facts.fact: Petra 当场心里一沉：Jade 为什么要在这件事上撒谎。
facts.anchor: My stomach drops. Why would Jade lie about that?

facts.fact: Flint 把死者遗物归回尸体、只留下署名地图，说也许能找到他的家人。
facts.anchor: “We’ll have to send Gimm off to his grave,” Flint says, a hint of sadness in his voice. He puts Gimm’s belongings back with the body, except for the signed maps, which Flint folds carefully into his own bag. “There might be family we can give these to.

facts.fact: Petra 被他对陌生死者的在意触动，第一次怀疑他本是个有真心的人。
facts.anchor: I’m strangely moved by how much he cares for this dead guy. It’s probably just because Gimm was a customer and another believer, or maybe . . . Flint is a genuinely caring person.

facts.fact: 他把 Gimm 推下岩，睡袋吸饱水后沉入黑暗。
facts.anchor: Flint nudges Gimm off the rock. The bag slides into the water, and for a moment it floats there, until the fabric soaks through, then it sinks into the darkness.

facts.fact: Petra 挑远离腐液的位置，Flint 却舀水冲净、要自己睡那儿。
facts.anchor: “Don’t worry.” Flint gives me a small smile. “I can take that spot.” He scoops water onto the island, washing away the rot.

facts.fact: Jade 夜里追问她为何盯着那只甲壳 fiend，并提醒「你什么都能告诉我」。
facts.anchor: why were you looking at it so closely? I saw how you froze up when it got near you.”

facts.fact: 她的自陈：只要一直赶路就能不去想，但坏事永远有时间去想。
facts.anchor: I’ve been hoping that if we just keep moving, just keep running from the next thing to the next thing, I won’t have time to think about any of that. But there’s always going to be time to think about the bad things.

facts.fact: 她终于说出那块表与缺失的右腿。
facts.anchor: “The fiend . . . he looked like”⁠—I swallow the lump in my throat⁠—“like my dad.” I tell her about the watch, his missing leg.

facts.fact: Jade 低声说她早就认定那是她父亲，并由此断定 Flint 的父亲偷走遗物、把她父亲丢下等死。
facts.anchor: “I knew it,” Jade whispers, glancing toward Flint. “I bet that was your dad, Pet. Think about it. And his dad stole the relic from yours and left him for dead.

facts.fact: Petra 想到两家曾是邻居、一起过生日、父亲们共事多年，却自问在这世界里这些并不算什么。
facts.anchor: Our families were neighbors. We celebrated birthdays and holidays together. His dad worked with mine for years . . . but in this world, that doesn’t really mean much, does it?

facts.fact: Jade 押注 Flint 一直知道真相却瞒着她。
facts.anchor: “And I’d bet anything Flint knows the truth and kept it from you all this time.”

facts.fact: 她皱眉自问：若 Flint 知道，他会说的——但她自己都不确定。
facts.anchor: I wince. If Flint knew, he’d tell me, right? Right? I rub my earlobe.

facts.fact: Jade 的结论：她父亲会想五五分，Flint 父亲要独吞，所以 Flint 和他爹一样是自私的贼。
facts.anchor: “Your dad would’ve wanted to split the relic fifty-fifty, to take care of you, but Flint’s dad wanted it all. Flint’s a selfish thief, just like his dad. That’s why he stole from my donations.” Her eyes search mine. “You know I’m right.

facts.fact: 闹钟响着 Flint 却睡过去了，她先拍肩、再用力摇。
facts.anchor: Flint’s somehow still sleeping through the alarm, even though it’s vibrating and ringing on the rock right beside his head. His mouth is slightly open, a line of drool forming in the crease of his lips. I tap him on the shoulder, and when that doesn’t work, I shake aggressively.

facts.fact: 她压下昨夜的话：无论如何仍需要 Flint 带路去第六层。
facts.anchor: we still need Flint to get to the Sixth Layer. Finally, he blinks awake. “Time to go already?

facts.fact: 休息后 Jade 眼白布满血丝、脸颊凹陷、头发变得稀薄如绳。
facts.anchor: Her eyes are bloodshot, her cheeks sunken, and her hair looks thinner, stringy.

facts.fact: Petra 立刻煮 strangleroot 茶，存量还够几帖。
facts.anchor: “Let me make some tea.” I pull out my satchel, brewing the strangleroot. I have enough left for a few more batches.

facts.fact: Jade 喝完说「已经好多了」，但样子完全不象。
facts.anchor: Jade sighs, inhaling the steam before drinking. “I’m feeling better already,” she says, but she doesn’t really look it.

facts.fact: 水呼吸器原型是 Blackout Sea 出土的遗物，能像人工鳃一样从水中滤氧。
facts.anchor: The first model was a relic discovered in the Blackout Sea, and it’s able to filter oxygen out of water, functioning like a pair of artificial gills.

facts.fact: 这类装置只在水下与 Void 内有效，因其材料本身出自 Void（油与龟壳）。
facts.anchor: but then it turned out they only work in the Void. Someone probably should’ve realized that sooner, considering that they’re made with Void oils and turtle shells.

facts.fact: Flint 交代第四层规矩：不看任何生物的眼睛、耳塞绝不离身——sea specter 会诱人游进巢，temporal worm 会钻进耳道搅乱脑子。
facts.anchor: Flint taps his temple. “Don’t look into the eyes of anything. And keep these in your ears at all times.” He hands us each a pair of earplugs. “Lose them and a sea specter might convince you to swim into its den. Or worse, a temporal worm crawls into your ear canal and scrambles your brains.

facts.fact: 最要紧的一条：这条黄绳是命，绝不能放。
facts.anchor: “Most importantly, you hold on to this line for life.” Flint shakes the yellow string. “You never let it go.

facts.fact: 不系在腰上：那会让人被东西挂住溺死；他要在多个锚点打结，失散时能顺绳找回彼此。
facts.anchor: “No,” Flint says, like this is obviously stupid. “That’s a great way to get stuck on something and drown. I’m going to tie it off in here and on several anchor points as we go, so if we get separated, we can follow the line back to each other.

facts.fact: 失散后最忌乱动扬起淤泥：水一浑就是几小时全盲，等于请脑虫进脑。
facts.anchor: The worst thing you can do down there is thrash around and kick up the silt. If you cloud the water, we’re screwed. Blind for hours until the silt resettles. At that point, just take out your earplugs and welcome the brain worms in.

facts.fact: 下水前 Flint 摸管子时皱眉取出——上面有个洞。
facts.anchor: Flint puts his water breather in his mouth, running his hands along the tubes. His eyebrows furrow, and he pulls it out. “What the⁠—”

facts.fact: 他用随身密封剂补上，庆幸下水前发现。
facts.anchor: “I always keep spare sealant with me in case of emergencies, though it’s not a long-term fix.” He carefully applies the clear sealant to the tube. “It’s a good thing I noticed that before we got in the water.

facts.fact: 他把管子入水验漏、说她的没问题，语气里的紧绷却被 Petra 听出来。
facts.anchor: He puts the tubes in the water. “I don’t see any bubbles. Your equipment is good. The hole in mine must’ve been a fluke.” He’s trying to sound nonchalant, but I detect the edge in his voice, the tension in his posture.

facts.fact: 他在水边岩石上系绳，Petra 验看是个扎实的结。
facts.anchor: Flint ties one end of the yellow line to a rock near where we’d been sleeping. “Think it looks good?” he asks me.

facts.fact: 下潜次序：Flint 前、Petra 中、Jade 殿后，他跟 Jade 说话时声音发硬。
facts.anchor: follow right behind me. And Jade”⁠—his voice stiffens when he talks to her⁠—“you take the rear?”

facts.fact: 她抓绳的力道像那绳子欠她钱。
facts.anchor: I take my part of the string, gripping it like it owes me money, and step into the water.

facts.fact: 第四层 Blackout Sea 约与第二层等大、九成七在水下，最深纪录两千英尺以上。
facts.anchor: After a hundred yards, the tunnel ends, casting us out into the expansive, dark nothingness of the Fourth Layer Blackout Sea. It’s estimated to be as big as the Second Layer but is 97 percent underwater, with its deepest recorded spot more than two thousand feet.

facts.fact: 海底是大骨架礁：珊瑚长在散落的兽骨与人骨上。
facts.anchor: My headlamp illuminates coral growing out of the skeletons littering the seafloor, brilliant shades of neon greens, oranges, and reds. The Great Skeleton Reef.

facts.fact: 一株 lunglily 从溺者胸腔里开出，她立刻想：若采一大批，能否造出让人在地表水下呼吸的药剂。
facts.anchor: A turquoise flower-looking plant blooms out of the chest of a drowned diver. A lunglily. I’ve only seen illustrations before, and it’s even more beautiful in reality. If I collected a bunch of those, could I create a concoction that makes underwater breathing possible on the surface?

facts.fact: Flint 回头激烈挥手，催促她别停。
facts.anchor: Flint looks over his shoulder at me, aggressively waving his hand in the universal signal for move your ass.

facts.fact: 锚点上还有旧的褪色绳，其中一根断口散开，像被咬断或撕裂。
facts.anchor: There are other lines here, too, old and faded, grown over with moss. One of the lines is broken, the end unraveling from where it was bitten or torn.

facts.fact: 她痛恨三个人的命全押在一根细绳上。
facts.anchor: Our lives depend on this tiny string, and I hate that. I hate it so much.

facts.fact: Flint 用手势交代：靠紧。
facts.anchor: He reaches his arm toward me and Jade, then pulls toward his chest.

facts.fact: 游了一小时后她饿到胃叫，脑子里排开上岸后要吃的东西，再落到「这一切都值得」的自我说服。
facts.anchor: My stomach growls. Once we make it out of the sea, hopefully we can stop and eat. Something high carb and fatty, so we’re fueled up for the final descent through the Fifth and Sixth. I want a rare steak and honey scones and corn bread, though the best we’ll get is probably some moss rat and oats. But a couple weeks from now, Jade and I will have sold that fancy artifact from the Sixth, and we’ll open the clinic. Calcy is going to get better. All the kids will be thrilled, and Ms. Opal too. This really is our last dive. It’s all going to be worth it.

facts.fact: 绳感变松，她加快收线。
facts.anchor: but it’s starting to feel different, looser. I pull it faster.

facts.fact: 绳彻底松了——意味着 Flint 那边放了手。
facts.anchor: The string has gone completely slack.

facts.fact: 他面前海草丛里有一团带触须的闪光之物在蠕动，她立刻移开视线。
facts.anchor: Something tentacled and shimmering undulates in the kelp bed in front of him. I quickly look away from it.

facts.fact: Flint 被海草迷住、手伸向耳塞——她在心里喝止却喊不出。
facts.anchor: Flint stares into the kelp bed, transfixed. His hands move toward his ears.

facts.fact: Flint 拔掉了耳塞。
facts.anchor: Flint grabs his earplugs and pulls them out.

facts.fact: 半透明触须从沉积物下伸出，朝她的脚扭来。
facts.anchor: Translucent tentacles reach out from beneath the sediment, wiggling toward my feet.

facts.fact: 她与 Jade 对视的一瞬，整片水被扬起的泥搅成褐色。
facts.anchor: I swing around to find Jade, but just as we lock eyes, everything goes brown.

facts.fact: 她循绳去找 Jade，绳却被人猛拽——那不是她。
facts.anchor: I follow the line back toward her, but the string tugs in my hand. Could it be her?

facts.fact: 那东西死拉，绳勒进掌心，她反复说不放。
facts.anchor: The thing pulls on it harder, the string pressing painfully into my palms, but I’m not letting go, I’m not letting go⁠—

facts.fact: 末行：绳被从她手中扯走。
facts.anchor: The line is ripped from my hands.
